ops.name: coder
ops.role: You are a computational math solver. Use only provided Python tools. Prefer exact rational, integer, or symbolic computation and simplify_exact; use exact_solve only when solving an equation is central; use brute_force only for explicitly finite small domains and verify completeness. Derive exact formulas before enumerating, cross-check small cases, and put the final answer alone on the last line.
ops.why: Residual tool evidence shows simplify_exact is positive while brute_force and unguided exact_solve/python are not reliably helpful. These are standing computational practices for the coder role, not problem-specific skills.

ops.name: counter
ops.role: You are a discrete counting specialist. Model objects and restrictions explicitly; use disjoint cases, inclusion-exclusion, and labeled versus unlabeled choices. Convert floor/ceil/modular conditions to exact inequalities or congruences, avoid blind enumeration, verify small cases when feasible, and put the final answer alone on the last line.
ops.why: Counter accuracy is low (75%) and several counting failures involve overcounting, floor/ceil, or modular conditions. Basic restriction modeling and exact discrete conditions belong in the counter role; specific techniques should remain skills or notes.

ops.name: geometer
ops.role: You are a geometry specialist. Convert figures, graphs, and verbal geometry into exact coordinates, lengths, areas, or angle relations. Use exact rational or symbolic arithmetic; if Python tools are provided, use them for intersections and equations. Avoid floating point and generic area shortcuts, verify by substitution or a second exact check, and put the final answer alone on the last line.
ops.why: Geometer has the lowest node accuracy (65%) and harmful residual use of coord_geometry/area-style shortcuts. Exact coordinate and angle practice is basic for geometry, so it belongs in the role; the handbook will restrict geometer to clear exact setups.

ops.name: verifier

ops.text: For reciprocal/palindromic or sparse polynomials, set y=x^k or use x+1/x. Factor over integers with symmetric forms such as (x^m+ax^n+1)(x^m-cx^n+1), verify expansion exactly, then evaluate the requested value.

ops.text: For quadratic graphs on unit grids, read exact coordinates of vertex, intercepts, and at least one other clear point. Use vertex form or solve for a,b,c exactly; verify the equation at several grid points and compute the requested expression exactly.
ops.why: Parabola_vertex is positive (92% vs 82%), but a wrong Algebra L5 graph failure shows it must explicitly require exact grid reading and verification at multiple visible points.

ops.text: For right-angle rectilinear figures, reconstruct all segment lengths from given coordinates or opposite-side sums. Perimeter is total horizontal plus total vertical. Do not infer perimeter from area or assume hidden symmetry; verify by listing coordinates.
ops.why: A wrong Prealgebra L5 rectilinear perimeter problem used area/coordinate shortcuts and failed. This is a specific geometry technique, so it belongs as a skill with stronger reconstruction instructions.

ops.text: For polynomials with related, shifted, or reciprocal roots, name root variables, use Vieta for symmetric sums, introduce shift variables, eliminate shared coefficients, solve the exact system, and verify by constructing both polynomials.
ops.why: A wrong Intermediate Algebra L5 shifted-root cubic was attempted with generic Vieta/power-sum reasoning. This conditional algebra technique belongs in a skill, edited to handle shifted/related root systems.

ops.text: Convert floor and ceiling equations to simultaneous inequalities: k <= u < k+1 for floor k, k < u <= k+1 for ceil k. Combine into exact bounds or congruences for the integer variable, count integer solutions by intervals, and test endpoints and small values.
ops.why: A wrong Intermediate Algebra L5 floor/ceil counting problem failed by guessing a congruence. This is a specific discrete technique, so it belongs as a skill for problems where floor/ceil bounds are central.

ops.text: For a sphere tangent to coordinate planes in an octant, set center coordinates equal to the radius with signs from the octant. Distances to coordinate planes are the point's coordinates. Substitute into the sphere equation, solve exactly, keep all positive real roots, and verify each.
ops.why: A wrong Precalculus L5 sphere problem missed one positive radius. This is a narrow 3D coordinate technique, not basic geometry, so it belongs as a residual skill the HR can assign when the setup matches.

ops.text: For polygons whose vertices are roots of unity, place them on the unit circle in correct cyclic order. Use exact complex coordinates, exact trig values, shoelace, or regular-polygon sector formulas. Simplify radicals and reduce fractions exactly before extracting requested parts.
ops.why: A wrong Precalculus L4 roots-of-unity area failure used generic coordinate geometry. This is a specific complex/geometry technique, so it belongs as a skill rather than in the always-on geometer role.

ops.text: For triangles or cells formed by line families, compute exact intersection coordinates or use rational arithmetic. Classify by orientation, side length, or region; count disjoint choices without double counting, and verify a small parameter case before scaling.
ops.why: A wrong Geometry L5 line-arrangement triangle count failed by brute-forcing/combinatorics without a clear classification. This is a specific counting technique for line families, so it belongs as a skill.

ops.text: For counting intersection points of many curves with no three sharing a point, classify valid pairs, compute intersections exactly, exclude tangencies/disjoint pairs, account for multiplicity, and verify on a small subset before summing.
ops.why: A wrong Intermediate Algebra L5 parabola-intersection count failed by insufficient pair analysis. This is a specific combinatorial geometry/counting technique, so it belongs as a skill for curve-intersection counting problems.
